data.name: Deacon
data.gender_notes: Deacon is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In early Christian communities, deacons were responsible for caring for the material needs of the congregation, freeing up the clergy to focus on prayer and preaching. The Greek word diakonos means ‘servant,’ and the title became synonymous with the role of a helper in the church. The name Deacon carries the meaning “Servant of the faith” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Deacon usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of the faith and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of service and dedication to the faith community
data.etymology: Deacon belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of the faith.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Deacon total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: דיאקון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: המילה דיאקון מקורה ביוונית ופירושה משרת או עוזר. בהקשר של הכנסייה הנוצרית, דיאקון הוא תפקיד רשמי המשרת את הקהילה ומסייע לכומר. הדיאקונים היו אחראים על שירותים שונים, כגון טיפול בעניים וסיוע בטקסים דתיים. הדיאקון נתפס כדמות רוחנית חשובה, המייצגת את ערכי הצניעות, השירות והמסירות.

in_greek.name: Διάκονος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όρος διάκονος προέρχεται από το ελληνικό διάκονος, που σημαίνει υπηρέτης ή διακομιστής. Στη Καινή Διαθήκη, ο διάκονος αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους πρώτους λειτουργούς της Εκκλησίας, που υπηρετούσε τις ανάγκες των πιστών, ιδιαίτερα των φτωχών και των χρεο负债τών. Ο διάκονος είχε σημαντικό ρόλο στη ζωή της Εκκλησίας, καθώς ήταν υπεύθυνος για τη διανομή των τροφίμων και την περίθαλψη των ασθενών.

in_latin.name: Diaconus
in_latin.long_meaning: The term diaconus is derived from the Greek διάκονος, meaning servant or minister. In the early Christian Church, a diaconus was a church officer responsible for various tasks, including serving the poor, assisting in worship services, and helping with administrative duties. The diaconus played a vital role in the spiritual and practical life of the Christian community.

in_english.name: Deacon
in_english.meaning: a church officer serving as assistant to the minister
in_english.long_meaning: The name Deacon originates from the Greek διάκονος (diakonos), meaning servant or minister. In Christianity, a deacon is a church officer who assists the minister and serves the congregation. Deacons are often responsible for tasks such as serving the poor, visiting the sick, and helping with worship services. The role of a deacon has evolved over time, but its spiritual significance remains an essential part of Christian tradition.

data.cultural_impact: Deacons played an essential role in the early Christian community as caretakers and ministers. They handled practical matters such as finances, welfare, and charitable works, assisting the priests and bishops in managing the daily operations of the church and carrying out the works of mercy.
data.spiritual_significance: Deacons' dedication to serving the needs and spiritual growth of their communities is an embodiment of the selfless love and compassion exemplified by Christ. Their role represents a deep desire to follow Jesus' example by living out their faith not only in prayer and worship but in acts of love and care for others. The office of a deacon instills a strong sense of stewardship, reminding us that all our possessions and talents are to be used to build up the body of Christ and minister to those in need.
data.spiritual_symbolism: A deacon is a servant-leader in the Christian community, entrusted with tasks that support the spiritual growth of the congregation. The name "deacon" itself comes from the Greek word diakonos, meaning "servant" or "helper".

biblical_reference.note: The term 'deacon' is mentioned in several New Testament passages, highlighting the role of deacons in the early Christian church.

historical_references.reference: In the Christian Church, a deacon is a person who has been ordained to serve the community in a specific way.
historical_references.context: Deacon is a title given to a person who has been ordained to serve the community in a specific way.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Deacon remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Deacon from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Deacon - "Servant of the faith". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
